detections.evidence_quote: No one had any idea if the gut was leaky.
detections.summary: Recounts the discovery and early research establishing that the gut can become 'leaky,' including pig and cell-culture studies on ATP and gut barrier integrity, and skepticism the concept faced from doctors.

detections.evidence_quote: there's all these articles by Harvard.
detections.summary: Cites published articles by Harvard-affiliated physicians on intestinal permeability to counter skeptics who denied leaky gut existed.

detections.evidence_quote: there's very little oxygen at the tip of the cells
detections.summary: Uses mechanistic language about oxygen, ATP, cytokines and gut barrier integrity to explain the leaky-gut findings.

detections.evidence_quote: I built a system using cells, not pigs
detections.summary: The leaky-gut findings were based on pig experiments and then a cell-culture model rather than human studies.
States that the early leaky-gut and ATP findings were published.

detections.evidence_quote: a repair enzyme inside the nucleus called PARP could get activated if your DNA is damaged
detections.summary: Explains a DNA-damage-repair enzyme (PARP) that, once activated, depletes NAD and then ATP; subject is a cellular energy/DNA-repair mechanism, not fitting any listed topic. Drawn from a Johns Hopkins neuro-injury research paper.

detections.evidence_quote: then if there was no NAD, then there would be no ATP that you could make
detections.summary: Describes the PARP-NAD-ATP depletion pathway following DNA damage using mechanistic biochemical language.

detections.evidence_quote: Paper coming out of Hopkins by Solomon Snyder's group.
detections.summary: References a paper out of Johns Hopkins from Solomon Snyder's lab as the source of the PARP/NAD idea.

detections.evidence_quote: Solomon Snyder is one of the great neuroscientists of the 20th century
detections.summary: Invokes Solomon Snyder's stature as one of the great 20th-century neuroscientists to lend authority to the finding.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Septic shock dramatically increases the leakiness of the gut.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: septic shock increases the leakiness of the gut quite dramatically
verification_candidates.rationale: A specific causal claim from early pig research linking septic shock to increased gut permeability that could be checked against the published literature.

verification_candidates.claim_text: A repair enzyme called PARP, located in the cell nucleus, can be activated when DNA is damaged.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: a repair enzyme inside the nucleus called PARP could get activated if your DNA is damaged
verification_candidates.rationale: A specific biochemical mechanism claim attributed to a research group that could be checked against the literature.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Giving cytokines that mimic inflammation to a gut cell monolayer causes a large increase in its permeability.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: we had a big leak in in the monolayer
verification_candidates.rationale: A specific causal claim from a cell-culture model that inflammatory cytokines increase gut barrier permeability, checkable against the published research.
